source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Access Redfish Endpoint:
    Access the Redfish API endpoint /redfish/v1/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog.
2. Check Date and Service Status:
    Verify that the "DateTimeLocalOffset" and "DateTime" match the BMC web interface.
    Ensure that "ServiceEnabled" is set to true.
3. Customize BMC Event Log:
    Log in to the BMC from the web interface.
    Go to "Events" → "Event Log".
    Open "Customize Table" and make sure all columns are selected, then click "OK".
4. Generate Events:
    Ensure that the system log contains at least one info, one warning, and one error event.
5. Access Redfish Log Entries:
    Access the Redfish API endpoint /redfish/v1/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog/Entries.
6. Compare Entries:
    Compare the entries in the "PlatformLog Entries" with the BMC web "Event Log".
    Verify that "Severity," "Source," "Message," "Created," "CommonEventID," "Serviceable," and "TotalSequenceNumber" match.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Critical content in Redfish and the WebGUI log should match.
Log entries with different severities (OK, Warning, Critical) should be verified and matched between Redfish and the BMC web interface.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: echo "=== LogServices collection (canonical: Managers/bmc) ==="; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices -H "Content-Type: application/json" | jq '.Members[]?"@odata.id"'; echo "=== sample entries per service (Journal/Dump/FaultLog known real on Wistron) ==="; for svc in Journal Dump FaultLog; do echo "### $svc"; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices/$svc/Entries" -H "Content-Type: application/json" | jq '.Entries?[:5] | [.[] | {Severity,Message,EntryType,Created}]'; done; echo "=== SEL/OEM count (Journal FaultLog) ==="; for svc in Journal FaultLog; do echo "### $svc"; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" "https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices/$svc/Entries" | jq '.Entries? // [] | [.[] | select((.EntryType // "") | test("SEL|OEM";"i"))] | length'; done
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: returns the LogServices collection + first 5 entries of each log service (Journal/Dump/FaultLog) + SEL/OEM count; user confirms remote-syslog/SEL entries present. Path per Wistron 11/12.RestAPI: /redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices{,/Journal|Dump|FaultLog,Entries}.

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES is unsafe and targets a different local resource set. It disables TLS verification, exposes credentials, samples only five entries, omits several required fields and WebUI comparison, generates no controlled severity events and collects no remote syslog receiver evidence. Its first jq filter is also unvalidated.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED improves path, field and event controls but silently reframes the case as local Redfish/WebGUI parity; it does not resolve why Items and Script say Remote Syslog or define remote delivery acceptance.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 831/2291 preserves YES based on command presence and repeats the title without noticing that the command, Procedure and Criteria never touch a remote receiver.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-994 draft was inspected only as history; this review independently retains BLOCKED/source-conflict and expands the severity, resource, Script and transport decision requirements.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 allows missing path/receiver values as readiness only after the purpose is known; ED-36 forbids claiming remote-syslog coverage from local logs. The conflicting target itself therefore requires an engineer decision.

original_test_intent: The preserved Items and Script identity say Remote Syslog, while the preserved Procedure and Criteria define only local BMC Redfish PlatformLog-to-WebGUI event-log parity across severity and metadata fields; the authoritative target is unresolved.
original_method: As written, the method discovers a specific local Redfish LogService, checks time/status, customizes WebUI columns, obtains events in three severity groups and compares Redfish entries with the BMC Web Event Log. It never configures a remote syslog destination or verifies receiver-side delivery.
manual_activity: Do not execute yet. Engineering must select or split the logging purposes and review the referenced Script. Afterwards an operator may configure/inspect WebUI and approve event stimuli; automation may collect all Redfish pages, receiver records and field comparisons for the approved scope.
required_inputs: Decision whether the authoritative case is remote syslog forwarding, local Redfish/WebGUI parity or two separately accepted checkpoints, while retaining all original identities and wording

For local parity: advertised Redfish resource URIs, WebUI authority, exact field availability/normalization, severity mapping between info/warning/error and OK/Warning/Critical, timestamp/timezone tolerance, pagination and retention
Approved uniquely identifiable events for each required severity, pre-existing-event policy and safe generation method without clearing evidence

For remote syslog: receiver address/identity, port, UDP/TCP/TLS transport, certificate/authentication, facility/severity filters, message format, timestamp/hostname/source mapping, delivery loss/order/duplicate and timeout criteria
Pinned accessible revision/hash of the internal remote-syslog Script and a step-to-checkpoint review
Protected credentials, trusted TLS, maintenance approval, alternate access, rollback and receiver/config cleanup
safety_requirements: Do not infer remote forwarding from local Redfish/WebUI presence. A remote-syslog PASS requires independent receiver-side receipt from the exact BMC.

Do not silently replace `/Systems/1/LogServices/PlatformLog` with `/Managers/bmc/LogServices/{Journal,Dump,FaultLog}` or vice versa. Discover and approve the platform's actual links and document coverage differences.
Do not use `curl -k` or command-line plaintext credentials; validate the BMC certificate/identity and use protected authentication.
Do not clear SEL, BMC, system or receiver logs. Preserve baseline history and use time/ID filters so existing evidence is not destroyed.

Do not generate warning/error/fault events until the exact reversible stimuli and abort conditions are approved. Existing entries may be used only if identity, time and origin satisfy the Project plan.
Collect all relevant paginated entries, not an arbitrary first five, and retain raw data before normalization. Empty or partial responses cannot be PASS.
The internal Script URL is preserved but inaccessible in this review. Do not execute or trust an unknown mutable revision until content, hash, parameters and recovery are reviewed.

Do not automatically retry event generation or forwarding; retries can create duplicates and hide loss. Stop on wrong target/receiver, certificate failure, log deletion, uncontrolled event or management impact.
agent_execution_scope: Before engineering resolution, only preserve evidence and analyze target/resource contradictions; do not access DUT, configure forwarding or generate events.
After approval, discover trusted Redfish links, collect every relevant page and correlate exact events to WebUI and, if selected, remote receiver records.
Report local parity and remote transport as separate outcomes even if one Project combines them into a single execution package.
Do not clear logs, use insecure TLS, choose event stimuli, retry automatically or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Decide whether to correct the scope to local parity, remote forwarding or two separate checkpoints and align the expected results without altering the preserved Master source.
Approve the canonical resources, severity/time/field mapping, remote receiver contract if applicable, safe events and pinned Script revision.
Observe WebUI/configuration, restore temporary state and issue separate verdicts for the selected checkpoints.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The read-only collection could inform resource discovery but cannot be accepted literally. It uses insecure TLS/secrets, different resources, incomplete fields and pagination, no WebUI comparison and no remote receiver; therefore it proves neither source interpretation.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No final command is valid until scope is resolved. Then use certificate-validated discovery and full pagination for local parity, plus receiver-side capture and transport/config evidence for any remote-syslog checkpoint, with protected credentials.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Remote Syslog Items/Script, Systems/1 PlatformLog paths, DateTime/offset/ServiceEnabled, all WebUI columns, required events/fields/severities and 20/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Split into (A) local Redfish/WebGUI parity and (B) remote-syslog forwarding unless engineering explicitly selects one. For each, use the same approved uniquely identified events, complete collection, time/severity normalization and independent endpoint evidence.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Engineer-approved BMC logging architecture, Redfish/WebUI implementation and optional remote syslog receiver.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, Redfish schema/service, browser, syslog client/receiver and Script revision/hash.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform Redfish LogService map, Web Event Log field definition and remote syslog forwarding/transport specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves two distinct functions, discovers actual resources rather than assuming paths and adds receiver-side proof for remote forwarding.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Local Redfish/WebUI equality does not prove any packet left the BMC; receiver receipt does not by itself prove every local UI/API field matches; sampling a different LogService cannot satisfy the named resource without approved equivalence.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Scope decision, resource/field/event matrix, receiver contract if selected, Script content, security, recovery and approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Mis-scoped evidence can yield a convincing but false PASS, while uncontrolled event generation or log clearing can destroy the records needed for correlation.

project_override_considerations: A Project Override may split the source into local-log parity and remote-syslog delivery, but must record the original combined identity, actual targets/methods, engineer approval, equivalence and any unexecuted checkpoint; it cannot label local-only evidence as remote coverage.
expected_evidence: Engineer scope/split decision, BMC/firmware identity and pinned reviewed Script revision/hash
For local parity: trusted Redfish resource discovery, complete raw paginated entries and WebUI captures for each approved severity
Per-event mapping of Severity, Source, Message, Created, CommonEventID, Serviceable and TotalSequenceNumber plus DateTime/offset/status and normalization notes
For remote forwarding if selected: redacted configuration, receiver/transport/TLS identity, network/server receipt for the same event IDs and delivery/order/duplicate timing
Preserved baseline and post-event logs with no deletion, restored configuration, final BMC/receiver health and engineer-owned separate verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Script identify Remote Syslog, but every Procedure and Criteria step compares local Redfish PlatformLog with the BMC WebGUI and defines no remote receiver or forwarding. The source and DeepSeek also name different unproven Redfish resource sets, and Procedure versus Criteria use different severity vocabularies that require an approved mapping.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Remote transport/delivery and local UI/API representation are different core operations with different endpoints and evidence. Selecting one by inference would falsely claim the other; an inaccessible Script name cannot resolve the target. Engineering must select or split the purpose before execution.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects YES and the different-resource local sampling shortcut as neither remote delivery nor complete local parity.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Changes its package classification to BLOCKED because it improved local parity safety but did not resolve the title/Script-versus-Procedure target conflict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Adds the missing purpose sanity check and receiver boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Independently confirms BLOCKED and expands resource, severity, Script and separate-verdict requirements.

review_improvement: Prevents local log presence from being mislabeled as remote syslog delivery and prevents a different vendor LogService sample from silently replacing the preserved PlatformLog/WebUI comparison.
independent_technical_reasoning: A remote syslog function is a transport pipeline ending at another system; local Redfish and WebUI are two representations inside the BMC. Matching those local views provides zero receiver-delivery evidence. Because the Master gives both identities but only one method, the target—not merely its parameters—is unresolved and meets the V3.1 BLOCKED threshold.
